=== F5 (BLOCKING, reproduced end to end). THE EXEMPTION COVERS THE FILES THAT DEFINE THE GATES, NOT JUST BOOKKEEPING. ===
The PR body says the change "only exempts pure bookkeeping commits under `reviews/`/`proof/`". That is not what `_is_record_only_commit` accepts. Its test is a literal `startswith("reviews/")` or `startswith("proof/")`, which also admits reviews/schema.json, proof/schema.json and proof/exempt.json. Those are not bookkeeping: reviews/schema.json is loaded and enforced by `_validate_against_schema`, and proof/exempt.json is the named-gap list lwb_check_proof.py reads to decide which merges may land with NO proof record at all.
MY REPRODUCTION, on a scratch clone at 4793afc, author `Probe Impostor <impostor@example.com>`:
  1. Edited reviews/schema.json alone, setting `required` to []. Committed; that commit touches nothing else.
  2. python scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py --base 4793afc --head HEAD -> "lwb-commit-identity check passed", EXIT 0.
  3. CONTROL, same author, same clone: a commit touching scripts/lwb_lanes.py instead -> EXIT 1, correctly rejected. So the check is not simply broken for this author.
  4. A/B to establish that THIS PR is what changes the answer: I dropped main's copies of BOTH scripts into the same working tree (so `REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` resolves identically) and re-ran step 2 -> "FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare or an allow-listed bot: Probe Impostor <impostor@example.com>", EXIT 1. Restoring this branch's copies -> passes again.
Net: after this PR, a commit under ANY author identity can rewrite the schema the review gate enforces, and lwb-commit-identity will not see it. commit-identity was the last gate that still looked at record-only commits.
I am NOT saying the exemption is wrong -- the asymmetry it fixes is real and well argued, and F1 is the proof that the asymmetry bites. I am saying its BOUNDARY is `reviews/` and `proof/` when it should be the RECORDS in them. Narrow fix: exempt only `reviews/<n>/*.json` and `proof/<n>.json`, leaving schema.json and exempt.json inside the gate.

=== NOT BLOCKING ===
n1. NO TESTS. The diff touches two shared gate scripts and adds no test. I measured 522 passed at this head; no existing test exercises IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS or the new `_authors` skip in either direction -- the stoplist and the skip are both invisible to the suite. The only evidence either works is probes in review records, which are not CI. Both are trivially testable: the four-case table above is a unit test almost verbatim.
n2. 'lwb' in IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS is inert: 3 characters against MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH = 8, so it could never have been a shared segment in the first place. I checked the lengths: buildcraft 10, leapware 8, lwb 3. Harmless, but the stoplist reads broader than it operates.
n3. A NEW EVASION THE STOPLIST OPENS, small but worth recording since this file is the decision record: a session that names its own token `buildcraft` or `leapware` now collides with nothing, because the segment is filtered before comparison. That is a deliberate act, not an accident, and reviews/README.md is already explicit that this check only raises the cost of an ACCIDENTAL self-review. Recording it so the next reader need not rediscover it.
n4. The `LWB-Agent: human` trailer on all three content commits means check_lanes does `if agent == "human": continue`, so this rewrite of the two scripts that ARE the merge gate required no independent review at all. I verified this rather than assuming: `python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --pr-number 40 --base bfe8507 --head HEAD` flags ONLY the record-only reviewer commits as needing review; the three content commits are skipped. The mechanism is documented in reviews/README.md and is not a bug. Whether the human exemption should cover a gate rewrite is an owner call and I am not charging it as a defect.

=== A NEAR-MISS I AM PRINTING RATHER THAN HIDING ===
When I first went to record this verdict I was about to name the RAW head 4af2b3e as `reviewed_commit`, because that is the tree I actually checked out and the literal head the REST API reports. That would have been wrong in the direction that matters: lwb_lanes compares `reviewed_commit` against the REVIEWABLE head, so a record naming 4af2b3e is rejected as STALE, and my verdict -- whatever it said -- would have counted for nothing while looking complete. I recomputed the reviewable-head walk myself before writing the field. I name 4793afcc because it is the commit whose content I judged, not because it is the value that clears the gate; the two coincide here, and had they not, I would have named what I reviewed and said so.
